RFC8654-3-1.note: New unit TestRFC8654ExtendedMessageSessionUsesRFC7606ErrorHandling runs on a live session that negotiated Extended Message (asserted) with UPDATEs over 4096 octets (1100 /24s). Positive: malformed ORIGIN length -> RFC 7606 treat-as-withdraw: no error, Established, no NOTIFICATION, all 1100 routes dispatched as withdrawn with no attributes. Negative: Total Attribute Length overruns the message -> RFC 7606 Section 3 b ("the Error Subcode MUST be set to Malformed Attribute List"): NOTIFICATION 3/1, Idle, nothing dispatched. Observed-red records: + revert enforceRFC7606, - revert rfc7606SessionReset. Replaces the old weak finding that only isolated ValidateUpdateRFC7606 calls were tagged; those stay as supplementary.

RFC8654-3-2.note: Code 6 is the whole obligation; row single-polarity positive (a fixed code has no refusal form). TestRFC8654ExtendedMessageWireIsCode6Length0 reads the octet WriteTo puts at a non-zero offset (06), Code()==6, and Parse(06 00) yields *ExtendedMessage: a code drift in WriteTo or in Parse's dispatch goes red. The old TestCapabilityCodeConstants tag (constant only) is supplementary. Judge 2026-09-30.

RFC8654-3-3.note: Positive: WriteTo writes exactly 06 00 with Len 2 and nothing beyond, Parse(06 00) accepted. Negative: TestRFC8654ExtendedMessageNonZeroLengthRefused sends code 6 with length 1 and 4 and requires ErrInvalidLength and no capability. Judge break: parseZeroLengthCapability accepting a non-zero length (len>8 guard) turned the negative red. Single-polarity marker removal is correct: a refusal path exists.

RFC8654-4-2.note: Non-compliant: an UPDATE on the wire larger than the negotiated maximum. TestSendUpdateWithSplitBoundsAnOversizePayload drives Peer.sendUpdateWithSplit with an over-4096 payload to a non-extended peer and asserts every wire frame length <= 4096 with the NLRI preserved; TestSendUpdateWithSplitTracksTheNegotiatedMaximum asserts the bound is 65535 when negotiated; BuildUnicastWithMaxSize refuses an oversize build (ErrUpdateTooLarge). Both polarities.

RFC8654-4-3.note: Non-compliant: an OPEN or KEEPALIVE allowed past 4096 because Extended Message was negotiated. TestValidateLengthWithMax requires an error for OPEN 4097 with extended=true (production gate: session_read.go:105 calls ValidateLengthWithMax); TestMaxMessageLength asserts OPEN and KEEPALIVE with extended both 4096, and UPDATE/NOTIFICATION/ROUTE-REFRESH 65535, covering the 'applies to all messages except' half.

RFC8654-5-1.note: Non-compliant: accepting a message over 4096 when the capability was not advertised. TestValidateLengthWithMax requires Error for UPDATE, NOTIFICATION and ROUTE-REFRESH of 4097 with extended=false and accepts 65535 with extended=true; production receive paths session_read.go:105 and session_coalesce.go:91 pass s.extendedMessage into the same gate.

RFC8654-5-4.note: Independently rejudged against rfc/full/rfc8654.txt Section 5 (lines 179-189): 'Similarly, any speaker that treats an improper BGP Extended Message as a fatal error MUST follow the error-handling procedures of [RFC4271].' Read the referenced RFC 4271 Sections 6 and 6.1: 'All errors detected while processing the Message Header MUST be indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Message Header Error.' Section 6.1 specifies Bad Message Length for the listed length violations and states: 'The Data field MUST contain the erroneous Length field.' Section 6 also defines closure: 'The phrase "the BGP connection is closed" means the TCP connection has been closed, the associated Adj-RIB-In has been cleared, and all resources for that BGP connection have been deallocated.' It continues: 'Entries in the Loc-RIB associated with the remote peer are marked as invalid.' Current internal/component/bgp/message/header_test.go::TestValidateLengthWithMax has distinct valid-length/no-error and bad-length/exact-code-subcode cases; message/rfc8654_length_bounds_test.go::TestRFC8654LengthBoundsPerTypeAndCapability additionally checks the exact erroneous Length Data. The current reactor/rfc8654_bad_length_session_test.go::TestRFC8654OverLengthUpdateFollowsRFC4271ErrorHandling establishes a session without capability 6, submits an all-ones-marker UPDATE header with Length 4097, and requires a ReadAndProcess error, wire NOTIFICATION type with code 1/subcode 2/Data 0x1001, then EOF rather than timeout. That input isolates the upper-length gate before body reading; the test genuinely discriminates notification contents and TCP closure. Producing source is message/header.go::ValidateLengthWithMax, reactor/session_read.go::readAndProcessMessage, reactor/session.go::logNotifyErr, reactor/session_write.go::sendNotification and sendNotificationWithin, and reactor/session_connection.go::closeConn. However, the tagged established-session fixture installs no routes and the test makes no assertions about Adj-RIB-In clearing, Loc-RIB invalidation, replacement/withdrawal propagation or resource release. A break retaining routes after this fatal error would therefore escape these tagged assertions. This is an evidence gap, not a finding that the wider routing lifecycle is absent; that lifecycle was not audited. Whole RFC 4271 fatal-error handling cannot truthfully be called enforced from wire notification plus EOF alone. Semantic audit change: enforced to weak for the imported closure obligations that remain unproven. The parent's minimum-Length tag correction is prose-only, changes no assertion or runtime behavior, and neither expands nor repairs this requirement's proof. No execution or new discrimination evidence is claimed.

RFC8654-6-1.note: Independently rejudged against both complete paragraphs of rfc/full/rfc8654.txt Section 6 (lines 198-206). The first paragraph states: '[RFC4271] states "The value of the Length field MUST always be at least 19 and no greater than 4096." This document changes the latter number to 65,535 for all messages except for OPEN and KEEPALIVE messages.' The second concludes: 'For all messages except for OPEN and KEEPALIVE messages, if the receiver has advertised the BGP Extended Message Capability, this document raises that limit to 65,535.' Current message/header_test.go::TestValidateLengthWithMax and message/rfc8654_length_bounds_test.go::TestRFC8654LengthBoundsPerTypeAndCapability (under internal/component/bgp/) genuinely distinguish accepted and rejected header lengths: OPEN 29, UPDATE 23, NOTIFICATION 21, KEEPALIVE 19 and ROUTE-REFRESH 23 are accepted in both boolean states; 0 and 18 are refused for all five types; 4096 is accepted for the four non-KEEPALIVE types without extension and 4097 refused for all five; UPDATE/NOTIFICATION/ROUTE-REFRESH accept 65535 with extension; OPEN refuses 4097 and 65535 even with extension. The header table additionally refuses KEEPALIVE 20. The bounds helper requires exact Message Header Error / Bad Message Length and the erroneous two-octet Length as Data. These tests isolate length validation and would catch the represented boundary regressions; they do not establish that the receive-side boolean represents the RFC's local-advertisement condition. Source evidence: message/header.go::ValidateLengthWithMax consumes a supplied boolean, reactor/session_read.go::readAndProcessMessage supplies s.extendedMessage, reactor/session_negotiate.go::negotiateWith sets it from s.negotiated.ExtendedMessage, and internal/core/bgp/capability/negotiated.go::Negotiate computes localExtMsg && remoteExtMsg. [INFERENCE from these producers, not an executed session] A fresh session with only the local speaker advertising the capability retains the 4096 receive bound although Section 6 raises it. Neither tagged unit exercises this asymmetric condition, so whole-requirement enforcement is unsupported. The corrected positive tag changes only prose, from Length 19 for every type to each tested type's minimum; the assertions did not change. ROUTE-REFRESH 23 is a valid tested message minimum, not a claim that Header.ValidateLength rejects 19-22 (that producer deliberately leaves body-length validation to the receive path). Semantic audit change: enforced to weak for the unproven receive-advertisement clause, not a behavioral regression attributed to the comment correction. No execution or new discrimination evidence is claimed.
